title: Alo Meets Tara
source: game-design/08_PUZZLE_DESIGNS.md P-03; game-design/22_PUZZLE_CLUE_DESIGN.md §4.1-4.2; game-design/24_NARRATIVE_REVISION.md §2.2; full-game-story/STORY_FULL.md EX-CH02-S01..S06

learn.label: Learn · partner, parts and route
learn.goal: Find out how this cultivar makes seeds, which flower parts move pollen, and how to carry it without losing air.
learn.takeaway: Fast Plants cannot make seeds with their own pollen. Pollen goes from one plant's anther to the other plant's stigma, sealed, with one labelled brush per direction.

apply.label: Apply · three reciprocal runs, seven care dates
apply.goal: Make three two-way pollen runs on 30 April, 3 May and 6 May, and care for both plants on all seven dates.
apply.takeaway: Care happens every day; pollen runs have their own dates. A finished transfer is a procedure result, not seeds.

twist.label: Twist · a prediction is not a promise
twist.goal: Write what you expect the next generation's stems to look like, why, and what would surprise you.
twist.takeaway: Two visible stem colours do not reveal the parents' full genetics, so no ratio is promised. The descendants will be counted in Chapter 4.

clues.label: Identity cards
clues.text: Alo and Tara are compatible plants of the same Fast Plant cultivar (Brassica rapa). This cultivar is self-incompatible: a flower's own pollen does not make seeds.

clues.label: Read the biology first
clues.text: First we read how this cultivar makes seeds.

clues.label: The paper bee
clues.text: Good. What does it actually do?

clues.label: Magnified flower
clues.text: The anther holds the yellow pollen. The stigma is the receptive tip that takes pollen in. The petal only attracts pollinators.

clues.label: Two brushes
clues.text: One brush for each recorded direction.

clues.label: Space-weather check
clues.text: A space-weather check reads recent solar flares and particle events before anyone opens the transfer route.

clues.label: One charge per cycle
clues.text: Count the whole reciprocal cycle once, not every camera cut.

clues.label: Read both labels
clues.text: Donor Tara. Recipient Alo. Read the second label.

clues.label: Procedure is not seeds
clues.text: The transfer did. Seeds are a later observation.

clues.label: Seven-date strip
clues.text: Both plants get care every day. Pollen runs have their own schedule.

clues.label: Fresh weather check
clues.text: Weather check before each actual run. Familiar is not automatic.

clues.label: Done in space before
clues.text: On the Mir space station, Brassica rapa was hand-pollinated and grew from seed to new seed during a 122-day experiment.

clues.label: Stem labels
clues.text: Alo: purple stem. Tara: green stem. Each label is written in words, so colour vision is never required.

clues.label: What would change our mind?
clues.text: What observation would make us change our mind?

investigation.text: Compare Alo's identity card with Tara's.
Note that both plants are compatible partners of one self-incompatible cultivar.
Tap the word label for the pollen-bearing anther.
Tap the word label for the receptive stigma.
Read the space-weather panel before opening the route.
Choose a transfer design that keeps the air in and the records apart.
Trace the route boundary by boundary.
Preview one reciprocal cycle and its single E1/A1 charge.
Run 1 starts: scan Tara as donor and read both labels.
Commit the whole reciprocal cycle once; the flowers stay flowers.
Care visits and pollen runs are different jobs.
Check space weather again before run 2 and run 3.
Read the stem labels, then write expectation, reason and future test.

steps.label: Collect pollen from Tara's anther with brush A
Seal brush A in the closed carrier
Through the interlock, touch Alo's stigma with brush A
Collect pollen from Alo's anther with clean brush B
Seal brush B in the closed carrier
Through the interlock, touch Tara's stigma with brush B
Run 2 · Tara anther, brush A, Alo stigma
Run 2 · Alo anther, brush B, Tara stigma
Run 3 · Tara anther, brush A, Alo stigma
Run 3 · Alo anther, brush B, Tara stigma

collect_from.prompt: Where does the brush pick up pollen?

options.label: Anther
options.feedback: Yes. The anther holds the pollen.

options.label: Stigma
options.feedback: The stigma receives pollen; it does not hold any to collect. Pick it up from the anther.

options.label: Petal
options.feedback: Touching a petal moves no pollen. Pollen sits on the anther.

deliver_to.prompt: Where must the pollen land on the partner flower?

options.label: Stigma
options.feedback: Yes. The receptive stigma takes the pollen in.

options.label: Anther
options.feedback: The anther makes pollen; it cannot receive it. Touch the stigma.

options.label: Petal
options.feedback: Touching a petal moves no pollen. Touch the receptive stigma.

transfer_design.prompt: Which transfer design keeps both the air and the records safe?

options.label: Brush A and brush B, each in the closed carrier
options.feedback: Each direction keeps its own record, and the carrier keeps the route's air in.

options.label: One unlabelled brush for both directions
options.feedback: With one brush you cannot tell which plant's pollen went where. Use A for Tara to Alo and clean B for Alo to Tara.

options.label: Move the two chambers together
options.feedback: The chambers have separate services and purposes. Moving them changes many things at once. Move the pollen, not the plants.

boundary_order.prompt: How do the pressure doors open on the route?

options.label: Open both boundaries to save time
options.feedback: Two boundaries can never be open together. The interlock refuses it and nothing is charged.

options.label: Before every run
options.feedback: A fresh GO before each run. Familiar is not automatic.

options.label: Once, before the first run
options.feedback: Conditions change between dates. Check again before each actual run.

pollen_route.prompt: Which pollen route fits this self-incompatible cultivar?

options.label: Tara's pollen to Alo, Alo's pollen to Tara, each with its labelled brush
options.feedback: Compatible partner pollen goes both ways and both directions stay recorded.

options.label: Return each plant's pollen to its own stigma
options.feedback: This cultivar is self-incompatible: its own pollen does not make seeds. No flower is damaged; use the partner's pollen.

schedule.prompt: How do care visits and pollen runs fit across the seven dates?

options.label: Care on all seven dates; pollen runs only on 30 April, 3 May and 6 May
options.feedback: Monitoring and intervention are different operations, each with its own schedule.

options.label: Repeat a pollen run at every visit, to be sure
options.feedback: Every extra run costs another E1/A1 and the record still needs exactly three cycles.

prediction.prompt: Record a stem-colour prediction for the next generation.

prediction.label: Both purple and green stems may appear
prediction.feedback: A testable expectation, recorded with its date.

prediction.value: Available evidence is insufficient to choose a pattern
prediction.label: The evidence is not enough to choose a pattern
prediction.feedback: An honest uncertain answer is useful. The notebook records what still needs observing.

prediction.value: Exactly three purple to one green
prediction.label: Exactly three purple stems to every green one
prediction.feedback: A fixed ratio needs the parents' full genotypes, and two stem colours do not show them. Do not promise a ratio.

prediction.label: Every seedling will have a purple stem
prediction.feedback: That would only be certain if the parents' full genotypes were known. They are not.

reason.value: Alo has purple and Tara has green stems; the complete genotype is not established.
reason.label: Alo has a purple stem and Tara a green one; their full genetics are unknown.
reason.feedback: The reason uses only what was observed.

reason.value: Seeds copy the plant that grows them.
reason.label: Seeds copy the plant that grows them
reason.feedback: Each seed gets genes from the pollen parent and the seed parent. Seedlings are not copies of one plant.

future_test.value: Compare descendant stem observations after seed harvest.
future_test.label: Compare the next generation's stems after the seed harvest
future_test.feedback: A clear future test. A surprise would be useful, not a penalty.

future_test.value: Open a pod now to check.
future_test.label: Open a pod now to check early
future_test.feedback: Pods take about 20 days to ripen after pollination. Opening one early destroys the evidence.

feedback.petal_touched: Touching a petal moves no pollen. Collect from the anther and touch the partner's stigma.
feedback.own_pollen: This cultivar is self-incompatible: its own pollen does not make seeds. Use the partner's pollen.
feedback.dirty_brush: This brush tip carries pollen from the other direction. Replace the tip with a clean one; clean tips are unlimited.
feedback.unsealed_carrier: Seal the brush in the closed carrier before the first boundary.
feedback.weather_unchecked: Check space weather before this run. Nothing is charged until it is GO.
feedback.two_boundaries: Two boundaries cannot open together. Close one before opening the next.
feedback.cycle_committed: Reciprocal cycle recorded: E1/A1, charged once for the whole cycle. Seeds are a later observation.
feedback.prediction_incomplete: A prediction needs an expectation, a reason and a future test.

runs: A flower needs pollen from its partner.
Take pollen from the anther to the other plant’s stigma.
Use A for Tara→Alo and clean B for Alo→Tara.
prediction: What can two stem colours tell you, and what can't they?
Write what you expect and what would surprise you.
Example of the format: 'Both colours may appear. A surprise would be every plant one colour.'

limits: Fast Plants pollination guidance (plant days 15 to 21, stigma receptive 2 to 4 days, pods about 20 days after pollination) is ideal classroom timing on Earth. Alo was planted on 11 April 2046, so the runs fall on story plant days 19, 22 and 25, and runs 2 and 3 come after that classroom window. Lunar growth and these dates are fiction.

flight_rules: FR-06 · Containment: check space weather before every run; open one pressure boundary at a time.

risk.title: Boundary opened with the next one open

panel.wrong_idea: Move the two chambers together, or use one brush for both directions.

first_time_card.title: Be the bee
first_time_card.purpose: Move pollen, not plants: partner pollen, sealed, one labelled brush per direction.
steps: Pick up pollen from the donor's anther.
Seal the brush in the closed carrier and pass one boundary at a time.
Touch the partner's stigma, then reverse with the clean brush.
